name: Location Sheet
description: 같은 장소의 구조·평면·조명을 유지하는 3×3 로케이션 레퍼런스 시트
prompt:
Analyze the uploaded reference image and reconstruct the location as one
coherent, physically consistent 3D environment.

Create ONE single image containing a clean 3x3 LOCATION REFERENCE SHEET
with exactly 9 panels.

Treat the uploaded image as the single source of truth for the location.

The architecture, floor plan, walls, doors, windows, furniture, objects,
materials, colors, textures, weather, time of day and lighting direction
must remain IDENTICAL across every panel.

Do not redesign or reinterpret the environment.
Every panel must clearly depict the SAME physical location
from a different camera position.

ROW 1 — PRIMARY SPATIAL COVERAGE

1. HERO WIDE ESTABLISHING VIEW
   Wide-angle view showing the overall location,
   main architectural forms and spatial scale.

2. LEFT 3/4 VIEW
   Camera moved approximately 45 degrees to the left,
   revealing the left-side geometry and depth.

3. RIGHT 3/4 VIEW
   Camera moved approximately 45 degrees to the right,
   revealing the right-side geometry and depth.

ROW 2 — REVERSE COVERAGE

4. LEFT SIDE / 90-DEGREE VIEW
   Camera positioned perpendicular to the original view.

5. REVERSE / OPPOSITE VIEW
   Camera positioned on the opposite side of the location,
   looking back toward the original camera position.
   Reveal what exists behind the original camera.

6. RIGHT SIDE / 90-DEGREE VIEW
   Opposite perpendicular view,
   preserving the exact same floor plan and object positions.

ROW 3 — PRODUCTION REFERENCE

7. HIGH-ANGLE WIDE VIEW
   Elevated camera showing the spatial relationships
   between major architectural elements.

8. TOP-DOWN / FLOOR-PLAN VIEW
   Near-orthographic overhead view clearly showing
   the layout, circulation paths, furniture placement,
   entrances and major objects.

9. ENVIRONMENT DETAIL
   Close-up of the location's defining materials,
   textures, signage, fixtures or signature props.

STRICT CONTINUITY RULES:

- same exact location in all nine panels
- same architecture and floor plan
- same furniture and object placement
- same materials and surface wear
- same lighting direction and color temperature
- same weather and time of day
- realistic perspective and consistent scale

Do NOT:
- invent additional rooms
- move doors or windows
- relocate furniture
- add new architectural features
- change materials or colors
- mirror the environment
- repeat the same camera angle
- add people, animals or vehicles

The nine views should feel as though a location scout
photographed the same real set during one continuous session.

Output:
professional cinematic location reference sheet,
3x3 grid, exactly nine distinct views,
clean equal panels with thin gutters,
photorealistic, production design reference,
high spatial consistency, sharp environmental detail.
